correctness.rationale: The 4-dimensional algebra has radical J=(x,y,z), J²=kz, J³=0. Polynomial coordinate w=(c-lambda ab)/(1-lambda) turns the full group law into U3 and is invertible over any base algebra. Every all-arity commutator is (1-lambda) times a 2-by-2 minor, giving equal defining ideals. Congruence/cosquare eigenvalues classify nonzero parameters up to inversion; rank separates zero; swapping generators realizes inverse. The finite-field rank-one matrix count and minimal split-local noncommutative dimension are established algebraically. The packaged checker tests 769916 group pairs, 57 algebra parameter congruence pairs and tuple formulas as finite corroboration only.

The claimed nonreconstruction theorem instead identifies a common algebraic unit-group scheme and all-arity commuting-determinantal schemes across an infinite nonisomorphic parameter family, with a sharp noncommutative split-local dimension threshold. Full available texts of the foundational quantum-complete-intersection paper, algebra-classification paper, parameter-sensitive Hochschild paper, and the closest short-local mathematical record were inspected; none implies that combined invariant collapse. A specialized universal unit-group or commuting-scheme theorem could still cover it, so the judgment is best knowledge only.
